problem: AgriVLN, the first agricultural VLN-CE method, reaches only SR 0.47 / NE 2.91 m on A2A, far below humans. In off-road agricultural scenes, whether a zone is traversable is ambiguous (e.g. an unripe cornfield may be traversable for a robotic dog but not for a human), unlike indoor or urban scenes, and the decision-maker has no explicit traversability cue.
motivation: Agricultural robots need reliable language-guided navigation on diverse off-road terrain. The authors hypothesize that ambiguous traversability is one reason for the gap between AgriVLN and humans. Rule-based and learning-based traversability estimators are seen as poorly suited to complex semantics and diverse geometry, so they use a zero-shot VLM-based estimator instead.
key_idea: After the decision-maker predicts FORWARD or STOP, segment the image with SAM2.1, let a VLM classify each segment as traversable or non-traversable for the given robot, and if the resulting traversability map conflicts with the action inside a trapezoidal alarming zone, re-prompt the decision-maker with the map.
insight: Explicit, robot-aware traversability information helps a VLM decision-maker fix its own mistakes in both directions: unsafe forward moves and premature stops. Ablations show both segmentation (SR 0.52 without) and the robot identity in the classifier (SR 0.51 without) contribute, against 0.54 for the full module and 0.47 without TEA. Gains are largest on clean terrain (villages SR 0.47→0.80, paved roads 0.43→0.56) and vanish on chaotic terrain (mountains, sparse plants), so segmentation quality is the bottleneck.
method: Segmentation (stage 1): SAM2.1-large produces instance masks; masks with area below τ_a=0.02 of the image are filtered out, and each remaining mask is overlaid with its index on the image.

Classification (stage 2): a zero-shot VLM (GPT-4.1-mini) receives the robot identity ("four-leg robotic dog"), the image and the overlaid images. It outputs thought, traversable IDs and non-traversable IDs, extracted by regex, and these are composed into a color-coded traversability map.

Alarm (stage 3): a trapezoidal alarming zone (t_z=0.32, b_z=0.4, h_z=0.1) is placed in front of the robot. The zone's traversable and non-traversable area proportions S+ and S- are computed. For FORWARD the alarm fires if S- > 0.1; for STOP it fires if S+ > 0.5 and S- < 0.1.
Backbone integration: AgriVLN's one-shot VLM decision-maker with the Subtask List module. TEA is a post-processing layer that stays silent on rotate actions and runs only on FORWARD or STOP.
Re-prompting: when the alarm is on, the same decision-maker is queried again with the traversability map and an extra sentence in the system prompt, and the new action replaces the old one.
Episode termination: STOP, deviation from the ground-truth action sequence over a threshold of δ=4 s, or reaching the max step limit.

setting.backbone: GPT-4.1 (LLM for subtask list) and GPT-4.1-mini (VLM decision-maker and traversability classifier), frozen via API; SAM2.1-large segmenter (pre-trained, frozen)
setting.training_data: none (training-free, zero-shot prompting of pre-trained models)
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: FORWARD, LEFT ROTATE, RIGHT ROTATE, STOP
setting.simulator: A2A benchmark, built from real-world agricultural videos and evaluated offline (no simulator specified)
setting.privileged: none (ground-truth action sequence is used only for the episode-termination deviation rule inherited from A2A)

numbers.evidence: Table 1 row 7, TEA-AgriVLN (Ours), A2A: SR 0.54, NE 2.70

numbers_note: A2A is not in the canonical benchmark list, so it is labeled other:A2A. The paper does not name an explicit split; 'test' is assumed. Scores are printed as fractions (0.54), not percentages. Ablation tables also report per-ground and per-scene results, not repeated here.
results: On A2A, TEA-AgriVLN improves over the AgriVLN baseline from SR 0.47 to 0.54 and NE 2.91 to 2.70 m, giving the best SR and second-best NE (DILLM-VLN has 2.60). Gains hold on both low- and high-complexity episodes (SR +0.08 each). Humans still reach SR 0.87.
limitations: Chaotic off-road terrain (sparse plants, mountains) yields poor segmentation, e.g. tree trunks vs fallen leaves, so TEA gives no gain there.
Depends on the frozen SAM2.1 segmenter and an API VLM, adding extra inference calls per FORWARD/STOP step, and thresholds are hand-set for a single robot type.
Evaluation is on a single benchmark; a large gap to human performance (0.54 vs 0.87 SR) remains.
